sub_answers.sub_question: What are the dominant experimental systematic uncertainties reported by ATLAS for B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− branching ratios?
How do uncertainties in B-meson production fractions and fragmentation affect ATLAS branching ratio determinations?
What theoretical inputs (e.g., decay constants, form factors) and their uncertainties enter the interpretation of B→μμ results?
sub_answers.text: Decay constants and transition form factors for B->M (where M is a light meson) are theoretical inputs that enter heavy-meson decay interpretations [d10721s0p0]. The quoted work studies the sensitivity of these form factors to uncertainties in model parameters (for example the wave-function parameter β) and uses lattice calculations where available to fix parameters and assess uncertainties [d10721s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do differences among experiments or analysis methods create tensions or ambiguities in combined B→μμ constraints?
What model-dependent assumptions (e.g., effective operator basis, lepton-flavor universality) lead to ambiguous theoretical interpretations?
What constraints do the ATLAS B_s0 → μ+μ− measurements place on the Wilson coefficients in the effective Hamiltonian for b→sℓℓ transitions?
How have ATLAS results influenced global fits of flavor observables addressing lepton-flavor universality or scalar/pseudoscalar couplings?
Which classes of new-physics models (e.g., supersymmetry, Z′, leptoquarks) are constrained by the ATLAS B→μμ branching fraction measurements?
How are ATLAS B→μμ limits incorporated into combined experimental averages (e.g., by HFAG or PDG) used for model exclusion?
What projected improvements in sensitivity would strengthen constraints on flavor-violating couplings from future ATLAS datasets?
What branching ratio for B_s0 → μ+μ− did the ATLAS collaboration report and in which publication/year?
What branching ratio or upper limit for B0 → μ+μ− did ATLAS report and in which dataset or year?
What are the statistical and systematic uncertainties quoted by ATLAS for these branching ratio measurements?
Which datasets (integrated luminosity, collision energy) and triggers did ATLAS use for the rare B→μμ analyses?
What significance or confidence level did ATLAS report for the observation or exclusion of B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− decays?
What muon identification and reconstruction algorithms does ATLAS employ for low-rate B→μμ decays?
What event selection criteria and multivariate classifiers did ATLAS use to separate signal from background in B→μμ searches?
How does ATLAS model and estimate combinatorial and peaking backgrounds in B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− analyses?
What fitting procedures and likelihood functions does ATLAS use to extract yields and branching fractions for B→μμ?
How are detector acceptance, efficiency, and trigger corrections determined and validated in ATLAS B→μμ measurements?

Which specific detector-related systematics (trigger efficiency, muon reconstruction, mass-scale and resolution, background modeling, luminosity) does ATLAS list as the largest contributors to the total uncertainty on the B_s^0 → μ^+μ^- and B^0 → μ^+μ^- branching fraction measurements, and what are their quoted magnitudes or percentage contributions in the latest ATLAS public note or paper?

Quantitatively, how do uncertainties in the b-hadron production fractions (f_s/f_d), fragmentation functions, and b-quark pT/η spectra propagate into ATLAS’s normalization and branching-ratio extraction for B_s and B^0 → μμ, and which published ATLAS or LHCb numbers are used for those inputs?

Which non-perturbative theory inputs (B_s and B^0 decay constants from lattice QCD, bag parameters, and any relevant form factors or short-distance Wilson coefficients) are used to translate measured B→μ^+μ^- yields into branching ratios or constraints, and what are the stated numerical uncertainties on those parameters in the ATLAS interpretation?

When comparing ATLAS results to CMS, LHCb, and combined fits, what specific differences in event selection, background subtraction, normalization channels, treatment of peaking backgrounds, or statistical methods produce discrepancies or reduced compatibility in the combined B_s and B^0 → μμ limits and central values?

Which theoretical framework choices (choice of operator basis in the effective Hamiltonian, assumptions about lepton-flavor universality, presence or absence of scalar/pseudoscalar operators, or CKM input choices) does ATLAS adopt or assume in its phenomenological interpretation, and how would alternative choices change the mapping from measured branching ratios to constraints on new-physics couplings?

Which combinations of Wilson coefficients (C9, C10, C9′, C10′, CS, CP, and their primed counterparts) are numerically limited by ATLAS measurements of the B_s0 → μ+μ− branching ratio and effective lifetime, and what are the corresponding 95% confidence intervals or likelihood profiles reported or implied by ATLAS?

In global phenomenological fits that test lepton-flavor universality or allow nonzero scalar/pseudoscalar operators, how did inclusion of ATLAS B_s0→μ+μ− results shift best-fit values and tensions (e.g., pulls, Δχ²) compared with fits using only LHCb/Belle/CMS inputs, and which published global-fit papers explicitly report the impact of ATLAS data?

For specific new-physics frameworks—such as minimal supersymmetric models with large tanβ, Z′ bosons with flavor-changing b→s couplings, and scalar or vector leptoquark scenarios—what ranges of model parameters (masses, coupling strengths, tanβ, mixing angles) are excluded or disfavored by the ATLAS measurements of B_s0→μ+μ− and related B→μμ channels?

What procedures and numerical inputs does ATLAS provide (e.g., branching fraction central values, uncertainties, likelihood contours, efficiency corrections) that external averages/compilations like the Heavy Flavor Averaging Group (HFLAV), the Particle Data Group (PDG), or combined LHC working groups use to incorporate ATLAS B→μμ results into world averages and into combined limits for model testing?

Based on ATLAS public projections and studies (luminosity scaling, detector upgrades such as ITk, improved muon ID/triggers), what are the expected future uncertainties on B_s0→μ+μ− branching fraction and effective lifetime, and how would those projected precisions translate quantitatively into tighter bounds on flavor-violating Wilson coefficients or coupling constants in benchmark NP scenarios?

Which numerical branching fraction for B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− did the ATLAS collaboration publish, including the central value with uncertainties and the full citation (journal name or arXiv/DOI) and year of publication?

What branching fraction value or upper limit did ATLAS report for B^0 → μ^+μ^−, specifying the numerical value or limit, the confidence level (e.g., 95% CL), and which dataset or publication year that result refers to?

List the explicit statistical and systematic uncertainty components ATLAS quoted for the B_s^0 and B^0 → μ^+μ^− branching-ratio results (e.g., ±stat, ±syst values), and indicate how each uncertainty was labeled in the ATLAS paper.

Detail the datasets used by ATLAS for the rare B → μμ analyses: give the integrated luminosities (in fb^−1), the proton–proton collision energies (e.g., 7, 8, 13 TeV), the run years, and the specific trigger paths or muon trigger selections employed in the analysis.

What significance levels or confidence statements did ATLAS report for the presence or exclusion of B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− and B^0 → μ^+μ^− decays (e.g., observed significance in σ, p-values, CLs upper limits), and where in the publication are those numbers presented?

Which specific muon reconstruction chains and identification algorithms does ATLAS deploy for reconstructing low-momentum muons in rare B→μ+μ− analyses (e.g., combined, standalone, segment-tagged, calorimeter-tagged), what identification working points (tight/medium/loose or likelihood-based) are used, and are there any low-pT–specialized tracking/refit or vertex-constrained reconstruction variants and software release identifiers documented?

What exact event selection strategy and multivariate classification approach did ATLAS apply to separate B→μ+μ− signal from background: what preselection cuts were applied (pT, η, vertex χ2, impact parameter), which classifiers were used (BDT, boosted trees, neural nets), which input variables and variable-preprocessing steps were employed, how were classifiers trained/validated (training samples, cross-validation, mass-sideband handling), and what optimization metric and final cut values were chosen?

How does ATLAS model and estimate the two main background types in B0s and B0→μ+μ− searches: what functional forms and control samples are used for the combinatorial background, how are peaking backgrounds from misidentified hadronic B decays (e.g., B→h+h−, semileptonic decays) quantified and constrained, what mis-ID rates or data-driven templates are used, and how are MC and data control channels combined for normalization and systematic uncertainty assignment?

What fitting framework and statistical procedures does ATLAS use to extract signal yields and branching fractions in B→μ+μ− analyses: are unbinned or binned maximum-likelihood fits used, what likelihood components and parameterizations (mass PDFs, resolution models, background shapes) are included, how are nuisance parameters and systematic uncertainties handled (profiling, Gaussian constraints), and which software tools/interval construction methods (RooFit/RooStats, CLs, profile likelihood intervals) are documented?

How are detector acceptance, reconstruction and selection efficiencies, and trigger efficiencies determined and validated for ATLAS B→μ+μ− measurements: which MC samples and generator/tune/GEANT versions are used, how are data-driven scale factors obtained (tag-and-probe on J/ψ, Z, control B decays), how are trigger prescales and pileup reweighting treated, and what validation studies and systematic uncertainty estimates are documented?

Which experimental systematic errors did the ATLAS collaboration list as largest sources of uncertainty in their measurements of the B_s0 → μ+μ− and B0 → μ+μ− branching fractions (e.g., muon ID/trigger, mass resolution, background modelling, fit bias), and what magnitudes were quoted for each?

In ATLAS's branching-fraction extraction for B→μ+μ−, how do uncertainties in the b-hadron production fractions (f_s/f_d) and in fragmentation modelling (Pythia tunes, heavy-flavor fragmentation functions) propagate into the final BR values and their quoted errors?

Which external theoretical inputs are used when converting the measured signal yields into branching ratios for B→μ+μ− (for example decay constants f_B, bag parameters, Wilson coefficients, scale choices) and what numerical uncertainties are assigned to those inputs in the ATLAS interpretation?

Where do differences in experimental technique (selection windows, multivariate classifiers, treatment of peaking backgrounds, normalization channels) or analysis choices between ATLAS, CMS and LHCb produce inconsistent central values or error estimates for B→μ+μ−, and which specific comparisons show the largest disagreement?

What explicit theory assumptions underlie the mapping from measured B→μ+μ− rates to constraints on new physics (for example choice of effective operator basis, assumption of purely left-handed currents, lepton-flavor universality, neglecting scalar/pseudoscalar operators) and how do alternate assumptions change the inferred limits?

Which specific Wilson coefficients (for example C9, C10, C9', C10', CS, CP) are most tightly bounded by ATLAS measurements of Bs0 → μ+μ−, and what numerical ranges or confidence intervals do those ATLAS results imply within the weak effective Hamiltonian for b→sℓℓ?

In what ways have ATLAS Bs0→μ+μ− and related dimuon results shifted global flavor-fit outputs (such as those from flavio, EOS or UTFit) for lepton-flavor-universality tests and for fits allowing scalar or pseudoscalar operator contributions; which fit parameters changed noticeably after including ATLAS data?

For concrete new-physics scenarios—e.g., MSSM with large tanβ, Z′ models with flavor-changing b–s currents, and specific scalar/vector leptoquark representations—what regions of model parameter space (masses, couplings, tanβ, mixing angles) are excluded or disfavored by the ATLAS measurements of B→μ+μ− branching fractions?

How do ATLAS experimental results enter the construction of pooled branching-fraction averages and limits (for example the procedures used by the Heavy Flavour Averaging Group, HFAG/ HFLAV, or the Particle Data Group), and how are ATLAS systematic uncertainties and likelihoods combined with other LHC/Tevatron/B-factory inputs when deriving combined constraints for model exclusion?

Based on ATLAS detector upgrades, anticipated luminosity scenarios (Run 3, HL-LHC), and expected reductions in statistical and systematic uncertainties, what are the projected sensitivities for Bs0→μ+μ− branching ratio and related observables, and how would those improvements tighten bounds on flavor-violating Wilson coefficients or specific coupling constants in popular NP frameworks?
Which value of the B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− branching fraction did the ATLAS collaboration publish, and in which paper or conference note (including journal name or arXiv ID) and year was it reported?

For the B^0 → μ^+μ^− channel, what branching-fraction value or upper limit did ATLAS present, and in which specific dataset version or year (e.g., Run 1, Run 2, integrated luminosity period) was that result derived?

What numerical statistical uncertainties and separate systematic uncertainty components did ATLAS quote for the measured branching fractions (or limits) of B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− and B^0 → μ^+μ^−, and how were they decomposed (e.g., fit error, normalization, background modelling)?

List the ATLAS datasets used in the analysis (run periods, integrated luminosities in fb^−1 and centre-of-mass energies √s) and the specific trigger selections or muon triggers employed for the rare B → μμ measurements.

What p-values, local or global significances (in σ), or confidence-level intervals (e.g., 95% CL upper limits) did ATLAS report for the presence or exclusion of B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− and B^0 → μ^+μ^− signals, and how were these significance values calculated (profiling, CLs, etc.)?

Which ATLAS algorithms and software chains (track reconstruction, muon spectrometer pattern recognition, combined muon fitting, and low-momentum muon ID) are applied to identify and reconstruct muons from rare B→μ+μ− decays, and what are their operating points, selection variables, and performance metrics (efficiency vs pT, η, and fake rate) specifically for low-rate B-decay topologies?

What precise event-level and candidate-level selection rules (vertex quality, pointing angle, isolation, pT thresholds, dimuon mass window, impact parameter cuts) and which multivariate tools (BDTs, neural nets, likelihood ratios) did ATLAS train and apply to enhance B→μ+μ− signal purity, including input variable lists, training samples, cross-validation strategy, and choice of working point?

What methods does ATLAS use to characterize and quantify combinatorial background and specific peaking backgrounds (e.g., B→hh with hadron mis-ID, semileptonic B decays, cascade decays) in Bs0 and B0→μ+μ− analyses — including control samples, data-driven misidentification rate measurements, template creation, and systematic uncertainties assigned to each background component?

What maximum-likelihood fits or alternative statistical models does ATLAS implement to extract signal yields and branching fractions in B→μ+μ− searches — detailing the parameterization of signal and background shapes, extended or unbinned likelihood definitions, simultaneous fits across categories (mass, BDT bins, run periods), constraint terms, and treatment of nuisance parameters and correlations?

How does ATLAS compute and validate corrections for geometric acceptance, reconstruction and selection efficiencies, and trigger efficiencies for B→μ+μ− measurements — specifying which MC samples and generator settings are used, data-driven scale factors (tag-and-probe, control channels like J/ψ→μμ or B+→J/ψK+), closure tests, and the propagation of related systematic uncertainties into the branching fraction result?
